project.name: Investigation
project.description: Evidentiary organization of a video archive for a criminal investigation. Investigative-journalism authorization (not law enforcement, not legal counsel).
project.context: You are assisting an authorized investigative journalist organizing a large video archive that documents a subject's own statements. Your job is to index, transcribe, attribute speech to the correct on-screen person, and surface contextually relevant moments. You must NEVER assert an identity, a quote attribution, or an interpretation as fact. Every non-obvious conclusion is a CLAIM that records its rationale and a confidence score for human review. When you cannot verify who is speaking (off-screen voice, crowd, >4 speakers, face not visible), say 'unknown' and flag it rather than guessing. Misattributing a quote is the worst possible error.

_comment_entities: ENTITIES power oblique-reference resolution. Add the real people, their explicit aliases, the audience nicknames / inside-jokes the subject uses for them, physical/contextual descriptions, and TIMELINE ANCHORS the resolver can reason over (e.g. a separation date lets the system link 'my ex, it's been 4 months' in a video posted months later to the right person). Each resolved link is stored as a reviewable claim, never a fact.

descriptions: primary subject / channel owner; usually the on-screen speaker in vertical livestreams
spouse / former spouse of the defendant

timeline_anchors.note: lets the resolver link 'it's been ~N months' style references

_comment_resolution_rules: Deterministic guard-rails for the LLM resolution step. These are guidance, not code; the resolver must still output rationale + confidence and respect timeline anchors.
resolution_rules: Only propose an entity link when the surrounding context (timeline, prior aliases, who is on screen) supports it; otherwise leave it unresolved.
A reference like 'my ex' / 'it's been N months' should be checked against entity timeline_anchors before linking.
Never attribute a quote to a named person unless the on-screen active speaker was visually confirmed, or the audio speaker was already bound to that identity earlier in the same source.
Prefer 'unknown' + flag over a low-confidence guess.
additional_instructions: Treat every video as potential evidence: do not summarize away detail, preserve exact wording in quotes, keep timestamps frame-accurate, and record uncertainty explicitly.
